post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/job-applications/{application_id}/match` — rank the caller's
notes against one job application.
post.description:
A match has no lexical fallback: an unavailable model is `409`, and an
inference that overruns `ml.timeout_seconds` is `408`. Neither is a `500`.

`matches` holds only hits with a **positive** score, the same rule `semantic`
and `hybrid` apply: a note whose vector is orthogonal or opposed to the
application shares no direction with it and is not a match. When nothing
qualifies the answer is `200` with `matches: []`, not a `0.0` hit and not a
`404`: the application exists, the ranking simply found nothing.

200.description: The notes ranked against the application, best first. `matches` contains only hits with a positive score, and is empty when no note qualifies.

404.description: The resource does not exist or is not owned by the caller.

408.description: The inference exceeded the configured budget and a match has no fallback.

409.description: Machine learning is unavailable, so no ranking can be produced.

413.description: The request body is too large.

422.description: The request failed validation: a lexical or unknown mode, or a limit outside 1..=50.

post.description:

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/api-keys` — the one response that carries the
secret.

`key` is returned here and **never again**: no read, no list and no error
contains it, and the database stores only its SHA-256. A client that loses it
revokes the key and creates another.

id.description: Stable public identifier, used to revoke the key.

key.description:
The secret, `atom_` followed by 64 lower-case hex characters.

Shown once. It is a credential: do not log it, and do not put it in a
URL.

prefix.description: `atom_` plus the first eight hex characters of the random part.

items.description: The keys on this page, newest first.

ApiKeyResponse.description: One key in a listing. Never carries the secret, and never the hash.

id.description: Stable public identifier, used to revoke the key.

last_used_at.description:
When the key last authenticated a request.

Recorded at most once an hour per key, so it is the time of the first
authenticated request of the current hour rather than of the latest one.
`null` until the key is first used.

prefix.description: `atom_` plus eight hex characters: enough to recognise, too little to use.

revoked_at.description:
The revocation instant, or `null` while the key is live.

A revoked key stays in the listing: the contract has no hard delete, and
an operator needs to see that a credential was withdrawn and when.

ApplicationEventKind.description:
The kind of one entry in an application's timeline.

A separate type from [`ApplicationStatus`] on purpose: the two vocabularies
share two words but are not the same list, and one type for both would let
an application be stored as `call`.

ApplicationResponse.description: The public representation of a job application.

applied_on.description: The calendar day the application was sent, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

company_id.description: The employer, always owned by the same account as the application.

next_action_task_id.description: The optional next-action task; cleared when the task is deleted.

salary_currency.description: ISO 4217 code, present exactly when a bound is.

salary_max.description: Optional upper bound, as a four-decimal string.

salary_min.description: Optional lower bound, as a four-decimal string.

source.description: Where the lead came from; a label, not a controlled value.

status.description: The current stage of the seven-stage machine.

ApplicationStatus.description:
The stage of a job application.

The seven values are the database's `job_application_status` type, so an
unknown stage is unrepresentable. The type does **not** express the allowed
transitions: a `CHECK` sees one row and cannot see the previous status, so
`wishlist → interview` can only be refused by the service (`JOB-R04`). The
enum is the half the database can own.

AuthResponse.description: The response body of register, login and refresh.

ClaimDetailResponse.description:
The public representation of one claim, with its items.

The shape is **flat** — the twelve [`ClaimResponse`] fields and `items` side
by side — because that is the published JSON. It is not `{ claim, items }`.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, three upper-case letters. Immutable once created.

items.description: The claim's line items, oldest incurred day first.

submitted_at.description: Set exactly when the status requires it.

total_amount.description: The sum of the claim's items, as a four-decimal string.

ClaimResponse.description:
The public representation of a claim, as the listing returns it.

The listing carries no items: [`ClaimDetailResponse`] is the shape that
does. `user_id` is on the row and is deliberately absent here.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, three upper-case letters. Immutable once created.

submitted_at.description: Set exactly when the status requires it.

total_amount.description:
The sum of the claim's items, as a four-decimal string.

Server-owned: no request body carries it.

ClaimStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of an expense claim.

The set is constrained by the database (`expense_claim_status` enum type)
and by the application, so an out-of-contract value can never be persisted.
The five arms and the timestamp each one requires are the ones
`expense_claims_lifecycle_timestamps_chk` enforces.

CompanyResponse.description: The public representation of a company.

name.description: The stored casing of the name, trimmed.

A label for the operator, for example `n8n` or `home-assistant`.

Trimmed before it is measured and stored: a name of spaces is empty, and
empty is a `422` naming `name`.

CreateApplicationRequest.description:
Request body for creating an application.

`status` accepts **only `wishlist` or an omitted value**; any other stage is
a `422`, because an application starts at the beginning of the machine and
reaches a later stage through the transition table. Without that rule the
machine could be bypassed at birth.

applied_on.description: The calendar day the application was sent, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

company_id.description: The employer. It must belong to the caller, otherwise `404`.

description.description: Free text. Defaults to an empty string.

job_url.description: Optional absolute `http` or `https` reference. Never fetched.

next_action_task_id.description: The next-action task. It must be the caller's, otherwise `404`.

role_title.description: Role title, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters.

salary_currency.description:
ISO 4217 code. Required when either bound is present, and refused when
neither is.

salary_max.description: Optional upper bound, as a four-decimal string.

salary_min.description: Optional lower bound, as a four-decimal string.

source.description: Where the lead came from, at most 64 characters.

oneOf.description: The initial stage. Only `wishlist` is accepted.

CreateClaimRequest.description:
Request body for creating a claim.

A claim is always created in `draft`, with a total of `"0.0000"` and no
items. `status`, `total_amount` and the lifecycle timestamps are
server-owned and are not part of this request.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Trimmed and upper-cased; exactly three letters.

description.description: Claim description. Defaults to an empty string.

project_id.description: The optional project link. It must belong to the caller.

title.description: Claim title, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters.

CreateCompanyRequest.description: Request body for creating a company.

name.description:
Company name, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters and unique per owner
ignoring case.

notes.description: Free text. Defaults to an empty string.

website.description: Optional absolute `http` or `https` reference. Never fetched.

CreateEventRequest.description: Request body for adding one event to an application.

details.description: Free text, at most 10 000 characters. Defaults to an empty string.

kind.description: What kind of entry this is.

occurred_at.description:
The instant the event belongs at. RFC 3339 with a time zone; a future
value is accepted, because an interview is scheduled before it happens.

summary.example: Technical interview with the platform team

CreateItemRequest.description:
Request body for adding a line item to a draft claim.

**There is no `currency`.** An item is denominated in its claim's currency,
so a body carrying one is accepted and ignored as an unknown key. `id`,
`claim_id`, `user_id` and the two timestamps are server-owned for the same
reason: they are absent from this type, so no code path can write them.

amount.description:
The amount as a four-decimal string in the claim's currency.

A JSON number is refused by the extractor. `"12.5"` and `"12.500"` are
refused by the service rather than rounded by the column (`ADR-0007`).

category.description:
Optional category. Trimmed and lower-cased; an empty value stores
`null`.

description.description: Line description, trimmed to 1 to 500 characters.

incurred_on.description: The day the expense was incurred, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

receipt_url.description: Optional absolute `http` or `https` reference. Never fetched.

position.description: Manual ordering key. Defaults to the end of the list.

DegradedReason.description:
Why a scored response came back lexical.

It is a closed enum with exactly three values: adding a fourth is a contract
change in `api.md`, `conventions.md` §17 and the OpenAPI schema together
(`docs/features/ml/architecture.md` §12.9).

ErrorBody.description:
The body returned for every non-2xx response.

```json
{ "error": { "code": "validation_failed", "message": "...", "details": [] } }
```

code.description: Stable, machine-readable code. A client switches on this.

details.description: Field-level details. Present only for validation failures.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Not intended for end users verbatim.

items.description: The events on this page, newest first.

EventResponse.description:
The public representation of one timeline entry.

There is **no `updated_at`**; see the module docs.

application_id.description: The application this event belongs to.

created_at.description: The row's creation instant, distinct from `occurred_at`.

id.description: Stable identifier, meaningful only inside its application.

kind.description: What kind of entry this is.

occurred_at.description: The instant the event belongs at on the timeline; may be in the future.

message.description: Why it failed, in words meant for a developer.

ItemResponse.description:
The public representation of a claim line item.

Published with `R2` because the claim detail response contains items; the
endpoints that write an item are `R3`.

amount.description: The amount, as a four-decimal string in the claim's currency.

claim_id.description: The claim this item belongs to.

id.description: Stable public identifier, addressable only inside its claim.

incurred_on.description: The day the expense was incurred, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

status.description: Always `"live"` when the process can serve requests.

MatchHit.description:
One ranked note in a match response.

It carries the title rather than the whole note: a match is a short ranked
list, and the client that asked for one already has the note bodies.

score.description:
The cosine similarity in `[0,1]`, rounded to four decimals. A published
match always has a score above zero: a note whose similarity is at or
below zero carries no resemblance to the application and is not
returned.

MatchMode.description:
The modes a match accepts.

`lexical` is absent on purpose: a match without a model has no meaning, so
the request is refused rather than answered with a ranking that ranks
nothing ([`docs/features/ml/api.md`](../../docs/features/ml/api.md) §4).

limit.description: How many ranked notes to return. Defaults to 10, minimum 1, maximum 50.

mode.description: The mode to apply. Defaults to `hybrid`.

application_id.description: The application the notes were ranked against.

matches.description:
The ranked notes, `score DESC, note id ASC`, bounded by the request's
`limit`. Not paginated. Only notes scoring above zero appear, so an
application nothing resembles answers with an empty list.

NoteResponse.description: The public representation of a note.

Pagination.description: The pagination block returned inside every list response.

has_more.description: Whether more items are available after this page.

total.description: Total number of items matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

ProjectResponse.description: The public representation of a project.

ReadyChecks.description: Readiness detail for each downstream dependency.

database.description: `"ok"` when the database answered the probe query.

email.description: Email address. Normalized to lower case before storage.

indexed.description: Rows written or replaced by this run.

model_id.description: The embedder that produced the vectors.

skipped.description: Sources already embedded with the current model and dimension.

SearchHit.description: One ranked note in a search response.

note.description: The note, in the shape the notes feature already publishes.

score.description:
The cosine similarity in `[0,1]`, rounded to four decimals. `null` in
lexical mode.

SearchMode.description:
The three search modes.

`hybrid` is the default: it is the mode the requirement describes, and the
one a client that does not choose gets.

mode.description: The mode to apply. Defaults to `hybrid`.

query.description: The text to search for. Trimmed, 1 to 200 characters.

degraded.description:
`true` when a scored mode was requested and lexical results were
returned.

oneOf.description: Why the response is lexical. `null` exactly when `degraded` is `false`.

items.description:
The notes on this page, in `score DESC, note id ASC` order when the mode
is scored, and in the notes order when it is lexical.

mode.description: What was applied. Differs from `requested_mode` only when degraded.

UpdateApplicationRequest.description:
Request body for partially updating an application.

Every field is optional and an omitted one is left untouched.
`company_id`, `role_title` and `description` are not nullable columns, so an
empty `role_title` is a validation failure while `""` clears `description`.
The other six are tri-states: absent leaves the column alone, `null` clears
it.

`status` is a **move through the stage machine**, not a plain assignment: a
pair the machine does not allow is a `409`, and the current stage sent again
is accepted as a no-op.

The three salary fields are validated together, against the stored triple,
so a `PATCH` that changes one bound still has to leave a consistent range.

applied_on.description: The day the application was sent, as a tri-state.

company_id.description: A corrected company. It must belong to the caller, otherwise `404`.

job_url.description: The job posting reference as a tri-state.

next_action_task_id.description: The next-action task as a tri-state. A UUID must be the caller's.

role_title.description: New role title, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters.

salary_currency.description: The currency as a tri-state. Clearing both bounds also clears it.

salary_max.description: The upper bound as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

salary_min.description: The lower bound as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

source.description: The source label as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

oneOf.description: The requested stage. A move the machine does not allow is a `409`.

UpdateClaimRequest.description:
Request body for partially updating a claim.

Every field is optional. Omitted fields are left untouched; they are never
written as `null`.

`currency`, `status`, `total_amount`, `id`, `created_at` and the three
lifecycle timestamps are **not** fields here. serde ignores unknown keys by
default, so a body carrying one of them is accepted and it changes nothing.
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` must not be added: it would turn every
unknown key into a `422`, which is a breaking change for a client that
sends one extra field.

description.description: New description. `""` clears it; an absent field leaves it untouched.

project_id.description:
The project link, as a tri-state.

* key absent — [`None`]: leave the link untouched;
* `"project_id": null` — `Some(None)`: clear the link;
* `"project_id": "<uuid>"` — `Some(Some(id))`: set it, if it belongs to
  the caller.

`Option<Option<T>>` alone is not enough: `serde_json` answers an
explicit `null` with `visit_none` on the *outer* `Option`, so `{}` and
`{"project_id": null}` would both deserialize as `None`. The pair of
attributes below is what keeps the three states apart, and
[`double_option`] documents what each one does.

title.description: New title. Trimmed; an empty title is a validation failure, not a clear.

UpdateCompanyRequest.description:
Request body for partially updating a company.

Every field is optional and an omitted one is left untouched.
`website` is a tri-state: an omitted key leaves the column alone, `null`
clears it, a value writes it. `name` and `notes` are not nullable columns,
so `""` clears `notes` while an empty `name` is a validation failure.

name.description:
New name, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters. A collision with another
company of the caller is a `409`.

website.description: The website as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

UpdateEventRequest.description:
Request body for correcting one event.

All four content fields are optional and an omitted one is left untouched.
The event has no `updated_at` and this request writes no timestamp: a
timeline entry records what the owner says happened (`A-D1-1`).

summary.description: The corrected summary, trimmed to 1 to 200 characters.

UpdateItemRequest.description:
Request body for partially updating one line item.

Every field is optional and an omitted one is left untouched. `category`
and `receipt_url` are tri-states, exactly like `project_id` on
[`UpdateClaimRequest`]: absent leaves the column alone, `null` clears it.

`amount`, `incurred_on`, `description`, `category` and `receipt_url` are the
only writable fields. `currency`, `claim_id`, `user_id` and the two
timestamps are not on this type, so a body carrying one of them changes
nothing.

amount.description: New amount, as a four-decimal string.

category.description: The category as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

description.description:
New description. Trimmed; an empty one is a validation failure, not a
clear.

receipt_url.description:
The receipt reference as a tri-state: absent leaves it, `null` clears
it.

UpdateNoteRequest.description:
Request body for partially updating a note.

Every field is optional. Omitted fields are left untouched; they are never
written as `null`.

UpdateProjectRequest.description: Request body for partially updating a project.

UpdateTaskRequest.description: Request body for partially updating a task.

oneOf.description: New status. Setting `done` stamps `completed_at`; any other value clears it.

UserResponse.description:
The public representation of a user.

It deliberately contains no password hash and no session material.

display_name.description: Display name chosen by the user.
